$schema-note: v1.0.0-recovery-testing skip-enforcement manifest (design.md §1.1, Task 0.4). This is the AUTHORITATIVE required set: 'required' lists the stable id of EVERY non-live crash/soak test that MUST execute-and-pass in the required gate (G9). check-required-tests.ts fails the gate by id if any required id is missing or reported skipped/todo/failed. 'deferred' lists WHERE-gated optional-feature ids that reconcile as skipped-pending-feature and are exempt while their feature is unshipped. Each governed test embeds its id as a [[id]] token in its title (which Vitest surfaces in assertionResults[].title/fullName). The Task-0 crash-harness smoke ids (crash-harness.smoke.*) plus the full T1/T2/T5/T3/soak/load-under-prune/P3 id set below form the contract that Tasks 1-6 tag their tests with; the ids are defined NOW so later tasks adopt them verbatim without a spec rewrite. CHANGE-LEVEL AUDIT (BLOCK 9): check-required-tests.ts now FAILS CLOSED (a missing/unparseable/empty-or-absent required set fails the gate, never reconciles as 'all 0 passed'), STRUCTURALLY PINS required.length to EXPECTED_REQUIRED_COUNT (currently 296) so silently deleting or adding a required entry fails the gate, and BINDS each required id to its 'file' so an id that executed-and-passed from a DIFFERENT file (a token moved to a trivial passing test) fails. The co-transactional saveAndAdvance crash test (crash.saveAndAdvance.co-tx-atomic, BLOCK 1) is required entry #23; the change-level round-3 differential negative-control (BLOCK 3) and reference import-clean (BLOCK 4) guards are required entries #24 and #25; every required entry MUST carry its bound 'file'.
$check-mechanism-note: IMPORTANT: run against the CURRENT Task-0-only suite, check-required-tests.ts will correctly report the not-yet-built required ids (the crash.* / soak.* / property.p3.* entries) as `missing` — those tests are authored by Tasks 1-6. That is EXPECTED and correct: check-required-tests.ts is the G9 RELEASE gate, green only once every task has landed its tagged tests. The check MECHANISM itself is proven independently, right now, by the synthetic-payload unit tests in check-required-tests.test.ts (which use an inline manifest, not this file), so those unit tests stay green regardless of how many required ids are still unbuilt. Do NOT delete a required id to make the check pass early — that would re-open the exact self-skip hole this manifest closes.

required.description: 0.1: spawn the crash worker, SIGKILL it, confirm the shared container is still up and a fresh client connects.
0.1: pg_terminate_backend drops a targeted backend's connection and the dedicated pool recovers (reconnects with a new backend pid).
0.3: a query against a deliberately-stalled backend is bounded by a 1.5s override of the suite watchdog and throws a typed SuiteWatchdogTimeoutError before G7's 120s, not a hang.
0.3: withSuiteWatchdog with NO explicit override applies SUITE_WATCHDOG_MS as its default bound (proven fast via fake timers, so the default is wired without a real 60s wait).
0.2: without UMBRADB_CRASH_HOOK the worker performs an ordinary uninterrupted save and exits 0.
0.2: the before-commit hook pauses after the manifest INSERT is issued, before COMMIT, and emits its readiness signal (incl. the worker backend pid); nothing is visible.
0.2: the in-critical-section hook pauses inside a held withLease; exactly one class-2 advisory lock with objid = hashtext(leaseKey) is held.
0.2: the after-data-commit-before-cursor hook runs TWO real ops (save then cursor) with a pause between; killed at the pause it leaves data durable and the cursor absent (watermark behind data).
0.2: the after-cursor-before-data hook runs TWO real ops (cursor then save) with a pause between; killed at the pause it leaves the cursor durable and the data absent (T5 unsafe reference case).

0.2 (test-honesty): the SAME co-transactional data->cursor flow run to completion WITHOUT a kill lands BOTH data and cursor — the negative control proving the killed T5 runs' absences are caused by the crash, not by a missing op.

T1 (Task 1.1): SIGKILL at before-commit leaves no complete=true manifest at the interrupted seq; the prior seq still loads+hash-verifies; no orphan junction rows; negative control (no kill => visible complete manifest).

T2 (Task 2.1): Postgres killed mid-save => the in-flight save rejects with a typed ConnectionError (not a raw driver error); after recovery the checkpoint is all-or-nothing and load(latest) returns correct bytes.

T2 (Task 2.2): the lost-COMMIT-ack state built by the sanctioned simulation (a provably-committed save re-invoked with identical content) yields a benign identical-content duplicate at the next seq; load(latest) correct either way; static check that save is excluded from any auto-retry allowlist.

T5 (Task 3.1, depends on G5): killed at after-data-commit-before-cursor, the durable watermark is never ahead of durable data (every write batch with cursor <= durable watermark is present in durable data).

T5 (Task 3.1, depends on G5): replay from the durable cursor converges on a current state equal (current-state equality predicate: kv_current + latest complete checkpoint payload + watermark values; excludes kv_history/version) to a fault-free in-repo reference replay of the same write-batch sequence.
T5 (Task 3.2, depends on G5): the watermark-never-ahead invariant holds under synchronous_commit = on.

T5 (Task 3.2, depends on G5): under synchronous_commit = off with an UNCLEAN postmaster kill (pg_ctl stop -m immediate / in-container kill -9), a lost tail of acknowledged commits is acceptable but an inverted durability order (cursor durable, data not) is a failure.
T3 (Task 4.1): after a lease-holder is SIGKILLed, a fresh process's withLease on the same key acquires immediately (bounded wait, no wedge) and pg_locks shows the class-2 advisory lock gone.

Soak (Task 5.1): a sustained concurrent mix at a declared envelope (10^5-10^6 chunks) samples a named P1-P10-derived SQL-observable invariant set DURING the run (gapless per-key version, only complete manifests loadable, no dangling junction, watermark <= max durable data); end state equals a fault-free reference; each GC-pass duration is recorded and bounded by GC_PASS_WATCHDOG_MS (no perf threshold gates).

Load-under-prune (Task 5.2): a FORCED, verified interleave lands the prune COMMIT inside load's open REPEATABLE READ snapshot window; load returns correct bytes and never raises ChunkIntegrityError/ChunkMissingError for a surviving checkpoint; negative control (un-snapshotted read of a reclaimed chunk DOES raise ChunkMissingError) fires.

P3 anchor (Task 6.1): the existing P3 replay/fold-equivalence property (getAt matches a from-scratch fold of the put sequence) is the differential gate's fold-equivalence anchor, satisfied WITHOUT importing the replaced store. Task 6.1 tags the existing P3 test with this id; no new test code.

Differential fault-schedule (Task 6.2, depends on G5): a SEEDED (reproducible, no Math.random) schedule mixing the G9 faults T1/T2/T5 across write batches, re-syncing from durable state after each fault, converges to a current state EQUAL (current-state predicate: full kv_current + full watermarks + latest complete checkpoint payload; excludes kv_history/version) to a fault-free in-repo reference run (a replay via UmbraDB's own adapters — NOT reference-merge.ts, which is transaction-history-merge only; no foreign consumer/indexer import, verified by an in-test import audit) of the same schedule. Mandatory negative control: a deliberately-broken variant that drops a committed range makes the equivalence assertion FIRE.

Co-transactional G5 crash (change-level audit BLOCK 1): saveAndAdvance — the single-transaction save+cursor combinator — SIGKILLed BETWEEN its internal checkpoint-data write and its cursor write (both inside the ONE uncommitted tx, paused via a test-only query observer over saveAndAdvance's own sql, NO src change) leaves NEITHER the checkpoint NOR the watermark advance durable (all-or-nothing), and a fresh saveAndAdvance on the same key then lands seq 1 committing both; a no-kill co-tx-full-flow control lands BOTH. Crash-tests G5 atomicity DIRECTLY (the two-transaction T5 tests never crash saveAndAdvance itself).

Differential negative control (change-level round-3 BLOCK 3): the mandatory dropped-range negative control - a deliberately-broken variant that skips one faulted batch's recovery so a committed range is genuinely dropped - makes the SAME current-state equality predicate the positive test relies on FIRE (throw). Required-enforced so deleting/skipping the control (or weakening assertCurrentStateEqual) turns the gate red by id.

Differential reference import-cleanliness (change-level round-3 BLOCK 4): a static audit that the in-repo reference imports nothing outside the repo - directly AND through its relative-import closure - catching bare import, dynamic import() and require(), and rejecting any @midnightntwrk/indexer/consumer/wallet specifier. Required-enforced so skipping/removing it turns the gate red by id.

--from/--to ingests exactly the range, records the archive start in the cursor, makes no request once the range is complete, and refuses a --from that would leave a gap or lies below the archive start.
every archived transaction's result and per-segment outcomes equal the indexer's (recorded Stagenet SUCCESS + synthetic PARTIAL_SUCCESS/FAILURE on real bytes).
an unknown TransactionResultStatus or a RegularTransaction without a result stops the sync at that block with nothing written for it.
429 (Retry-After) / 403 / 503 / an HTML 200 from the endpoints are retried with back-off, counted, and the range still completes.

SIGKILL of the CLI during a --from/--to run, then a restart, leaves every archive table identical to an uninterrupted run (wall-clock columns excluded); the cursor never runs ahead of or behind the data.
transactions.segments round-trips next to result (sorted, null = no list); malformed lists are rejected by the store and by the transactions_segments_shape CHECK.
putBlockBundle's watermark commits with the block, rolls back with a failed bundle, and never moves backwards.
the pinned ledger-v9 decodes every recorded Stagenet case transaction (hash, actions, mint effects) and rawTokenType reproduces the IDX/U1 colors.
every vendored MIP-0018 reference file (codec, vectors, runner; daec1f1) equals its SHA-256 in token-indexer/vendor/mip0018/SOURCE.md; a modified, missing or unlisted file fails.
the vendored MIP-0018 vectors pass their own SHA256SUMS, as the runner checks before a run.

the mip0018 migration lineage creates exactly its tables (event log, latest-value fields, withdrawals, listed events, scan cursor, mints, color sightings, contract actions, built-in tokens, activity; no history table) and re-running is a no-op.
keys and values are exact bytea (NUL and non-UTF-8 keys) and a 31-byte unsigned integer is lossless.
the schema refuses stored tombstones, kinds outside 1-3, unsized integers and accepted events without a header.

per-key tombstones (MIP 274a84f): a Null deletes only its key, a Null for a missing key is a no-op, deleting every key leaves the identity absent from listings, lookups, groups and display, a later record revives only that field.
the mark function (ok / partial / incorrect with reasons / unresolved / none; precedence incorrect, unresolved, fields; usable standards as tags).
Pure adapter: 59/59 reference normative + 43/43 informative vendored vectors and UmbraDB's 8 own versions (S1a, S3a-S3d, S4a/S4b, S9d; MIP 274a84f) pass through the vendored runner core.
the vendored 78ecbb4 versions of exactly S3a, S3b, S3c, S3d, S4b, S9d fail under per-key tombstones (why UmbraDB runs its own versions).
UmbraDB's own vectors match their SHA256SUMS and their generator's --check.
the vendored runner CLI drives the pure adapter process over both vector sets and exits 0.
every recorded Stagenet fixture file matches its manifest SHA-256 and size; provenance (endpoints, genesis, queries) and the < 1 MB size target hold.

the IDX (714485-715183) and U1 (715402-715433) tapes are contiguous, node and indexer answers agree, and every (transaction, called contract) pair has its contractEvents capture in the indexer's order.
every C01-C10/IDX/U1 reference case transaction is in the tapes at its height and position, and its observed indexer event ids are in the contractEvents capture.
replaying each recorded range through the unchanged chain-archive-sync into Postgres reproduces the archive digest of the live polite sync taken at capture time.

the applied-parts decoder lists logs, mints, deploys, maintenance and colors in the ledger's execution order (guaranteed part of every intent by ascending segment, then each fallible segment) and zero-extends trimmed Misc data to 288 bytes.
only applied parts count — FAILURE applies nothing, PARTIAL_SUCCESS keeps the guaranteed part and the successful segments (a segment missing from the list counts as failed).
an unknown contract action, unreadable bytes or a log of another shape is reported, never skipped silently.
recorded Stagenet mints give the reference colors, contracts, domainSeps and kinds (kinds 1 and 2 of C04 share one color) and every wallet-observed color of C02-C05/U1.
recorded deploys, maintenance updates (C10 VerifierKeyRemove, U1 VerifierKeyInsert), the two-call transaction of 714813 and C10's 127-byte raw item are decoded.
the scan of C04's archived range gives one color for its shielded and unshielded mints, its deploy and calls, and the NIGHT/DUST rows.
the recorded IDX range 714485-715183 gives exactly the reference's 6 colors (C05 bronze not minted), U1's range its color; 60 call actions in 58 transactions, 9 deploys, 1 maintenance update.
a FAILURE transaction and a failed fallible segment add no mint, color, sighting or action; the guaranteed part of a partial success does.
a color seen in public data before its mint is listed as seen, then completed in place by the mint.
batches, restarts and a crash inside a block give the same tables as one uninterrupted scan; a cursor moved by another writer is refused.
removing everything above a height and scanning again gives the same tables.
--from/--to, the archive's end and inconsistent archive rows (gap, parent, result, hash, undecodable) stop the scan with an error.
the scan CLI scans an archived range to --to and resumes at its cursor.
every Misc event of the recorded ranges is stored with its classification — C07 9/9/4 step by step, C08 1/1/0, the reference IDX scan's 35 v1 events position by position, other names ignored.
events follow the MIP order within a transaction (recorded C04; synthetic intents and segments); failed segments and FAILURE transactions add nothing.
C10's event, a 127-byte raw ledger item, is stored and decoded as MIP Appendix A's full 32 + 256 bytes.
raw-derived events equal the indexer's recorded contractEvents for every (transaction, called contract) pair — same events, order, bytes and segment.
a withdrawn identity is marked exactly like one never described — from its contract's rejections only; an empty field map is the same as none.
negative control — a consumer reporting no groups passes the runner only with S3a, S3b, S4a, S9d (and the vendored S9a–S9c) not applicable, which the adapter tests refuse.
59/59 reference normative + 43/43 informative + 8/8 UmbraDB vectors through the Postgres write path and read helpers, no check not applicable, every response equal to the pure adapter's.
the vendored runner CLI drives the Postgres adapter process over both vector sets and exits 0 with every check applicable.
every recorded case's state equals its expectation (reference files, SHA-256 checked; C06 UmbraDB's per-key state); a full recompute from the log changes nothing.
symbol groups on the recorded ranges are exactly C04's ACD and C05's MEDAL; no single-member group.
MIP S4 on chain: C06 step by step equals the reference (publish, rename) and UmbraDB's per-key expectations (withdraw, withdraw again, revive); removing and re-adding the tombstone block.
withdrawing one of two identities of a contract leaves the shared entries, withdrawing the last removes them; mints stay; a revive sets only its field; removeAbove restores both.
C07's NUL, non-UTF-8, 220-byte keys and 219-byte values round-trip as bytes; a 31-byte integer is lossless.
C01/C10 ✓, C07/C08 ⚠ incorrect with reasons, a partial token ⚠ partial, a minted token without events no mark, a withdrawn identity marked from its contract's rejections only.
a crash inside the C06 tombstone block rolls back its fields; batches, restarts and the crash give tables (fields included) identical to an uninterrupted scan.
Bech32m codec passes BIP-350's valid/invalid strings and segwit vectors at the Bech32m layer.
C03's recorded mint output encodes to wallet 1's recorded mn_addr_stagenet address; recorded addresses round-trip; HRP rule; refusals.
C03's mint row shows mn_addr_stagenet1vw57…; its UTXO (intentHash(0)) and metadata transaction follow in chain order.
C06's five metadata transactions at their heights without values; keyset pages in both orders; bad requests refused.
on the recorded IDX/U1 ranges each color's activity = its case's transactions; mint rows = mint table; metadata rows = event log.
nothing of a failed segment or FAILURE transaction; all public flows of a success (spends, outputs, NIGHT, contract in/out, deltas); recipient rules.
removeAbove deletes activity above a height; a rescan restores it exactly.
the scan CLI SIGKILLed inside a block transaction leaves none of its rows; a restart equals an uninterrupted scan.

/v1/status serves network, genesis (= the recorded fixture's), start/indexed/archive heights, the MIP pin 274a84f and the vendored commit daec1f1 (checked against SOURCE.md and the own vectors' manifest).

/v1/tokens = NIGHT, DUST, every minted or described identity in byte order with usable name/symbol/decimals, mark and tags; keyset pages of any size walk to the same list; bad limits and foreign cursors are 400.
token by color, identity and contract tokens with fields (hex + text/integer views, usable), groups of two or more, marks; C07's exact bytes incl. NUL and non-UTF-8 keys; 404s.
MIP Lookup: C04's color resolves to kind 1 held shielded and kind 2 held unshielded; C05 bronze is not minted in the indexed range; NIGHT's zero color is the built-in row; held is required.
/v1/events serves accept/reject events of a contract or transaction in chain order with position, contract, classification and reason only; ignored events and stored bytes are never served.
C01 ok, C07 and C08 incorrect with their reasons, a partial identity partial, a minted token without events unmarked, NIGHT/DUST without a mark — through the API.

MIP 274a84f Applying records: after C06's tombstone the withdrawn name is absent from every endpoint; a wholly withdrawn identity is 404 and appears nowhere; a withdrawn minted identity reads like a never-described one.

MIP Consuming: bidi/invisible/control characters, markup and non-UTF-8 bytes are served as data in pure-ASCII JSON that parses back exactly; non-UTF-8 only as hex; hostile contract entry points (NUL, non-UTF-8, bidi) never stop the scan and are served as exact hex, text only when printable; the API modules hold no network client.
400/404/405/503 error envelope without input echo or internal details; strict hex lengths, kinds 1-3, parameters; HEAD answers headers only.
serve binds 127.0.0.1, runs the scan loop following the archive (or API only), logs the bound port, exits 0 on SIGTERM, refuses bad arguments.

/v1/tokens/{color}/activity and /v1/contracts/{address}/activity serve the stored activity rows; C03's mint row and UTXO carry wallet 1 in Bech32m (never hex); C06's five metadata transactions at their heights; keyset pages in both orders; 400/404.

the served page parses, its CSP hashes are its inline script/style bytes, the script compiles (stray-backtick negative control), pure ASCII, no handler/style/src attribute or external reference, no markup sink, clock or other network client, only /v1 API paths.
serve() answers /ui, the font, the icon and / -> /ui from the API server; other methods and unknown /ui paths fall through to the API; no page without the hook; font licence in NOTICE.

real headless browser on the recorded IDX range: NIGHT/DUST first, every API row with its mark and tags, every route renders, activity as the API answers, only same-origin page/API requests, no CSP violation or console error.

the activity section draws what the real activity endpoints answer: C03's UTXO and mint rows with wallet 1 in Bech32m (never hex) and its publish, C06's five metadata transactions on the identity and contract views; on synthetic blocks through the real scanner every role, Bech32m wallets, a hostile entry point as its hex (never decoded text), and load more with the API's cursor.

MIP Security considerations: bidi/zero-width/NUL/control characters and every Cc/Cf/Co/Cn/Cs/Zl/Zp/Default_Ignorable code point incl. U+1BCA0, U+180F and U+0600-U+0605 drawn as visible marks (never raw, not in tooltips; a look-alike symbol told apart), markup as text, URIs never fetched or linked, budgets with show all, unusable field without its value; hostile contract entry points drawn as their hex, a printable one as text.
MIP Applying records: with the page refreshing on its own, C06's withdrawn name and a synthetic wholly withdrawn identity appear on no reachable view; its direct route says no such identity.
each Stagenet case replayed up to its own last block equals its expectation (later cases absent, earlier ones unchanged); C09 leaves C01's state unchanged; U1 at its last block.

IDX and U1 equal the reference's own index files (expected.json colors and identities, index-summary colors/mints, deploys, v1 events with position and classification, stats, last block); exactly 6 IDX colors, C05 bronze not minted.

every case identity's mark and standards tags (range end and each C06 step) equal the mark rule applied to the reference expectations and the reference index's rejections; the third party's minted token has no mark.
every case contract's metadata transactions equal the transactions the reference index lists for it, with their counts; C05 bronze has no color activity.

a replay of the recorded 714485-715183 tape through the sync service and the scanner equals, table by table (archive and mip0018), the digests recorded from the live Stagenet sync (that uninterrupted live run = the replay); a changed row is caught.

token-indexer/CONFORMANCE.md lists exactly the 36 MUST/SHOULD requirements of MIP 274a84f (SHA-256 of the extracted list), each covered or not applicable with a reason; every cited test id, vector and path exists.

the indexer's runtime code and the vendored codec contain no network client, no dynamic code and no child process (MIP C-024, C-031); positive controls for every forbidden form; every module loaded through the runtime's relative import closure is on an exact allowlist, with negative controls (axios, undici, got, node:net, child_process, dynamic package imports, a path into node_modules).

Entry points are arbitrary bytes (ledger maybe_str): calls and maintenance updates naming NUL, non-UTF-8, bidi or empty entry points never stop the scan; their exact bytes are stored as bytea in mip0018_contract_actions and mip0018_activity; maintenance_updates stays ASCII; hex + text only when printable; negative controls (text refuses NUL, UTF-8 decode is lossy).

every text column of the mip0018 lineage is classified (operator configuration, fixed vocabulary, code-generated ASCII, code constant); entry points and other chain byte strings are bytea; event_type, reason and maintenance_updates refuse anything but printable ASCII; a NUL cannot reach a text column.

logged values follow the ledger's decode_event (a well-formed [u32, LogEventType, data] triple has its type, any other value is Misc version 0 with the whole value as data, a single cell split name || payload after zero-extension); the transcript program's forward-only branch/jmp control flow decides whether a log op is resolved (operand pushed right before it, on every successful path), unresolved (operand not pushed, or conditionally executed) or never run.

through the real scan and API, a bare logged value is applied as a Misc event; a log op whose value the raw transaction does not show is stored as unresolved with its reason, never applied, served in /v1/events and counted in /v1/status; a never-run log op leaves no row; the scan never stops on them.

MIP 'Applying records': a withdrawn identity is not referenced in metadata history: a color's and a contract's activity list metadata transactions only for rejected events and accepted events of an identity's current description; a withdrawn native token's publish and withdrawal transactions disappear while its mints stay; a sibling's rows stay until it is withdrawn; a revived identity's history starts at its revival; removeAbove restores the earlier listings; C06's per-key steps keep every row.

a reader paging /v1/tokens never loses a token that existed when paging began: a color seen before its first mint keeps its seen row (same key) after the mint is indexed while its identity row appears; a color first seen in its own mint transaction is never a seen row.

with an identity of 50 000 keys, 50 000 rejected and 50 000 ignored events of its contract, a 2 001-member symbol group and a 100 000-byte entry point, every API answer stays small and within a generous latency budget: list rows and marks read only the common keys and the first 100 reasons (reasonCount = all), identity fields come in keyset pages with fieldCount, groups list 100 members with memberCount, events page over served rows only, entry points are served as 128 bytes plus their length.

at most maxConcurrentRequests API requests run at once (default 8, below the pool's 10); the next is answered at once with 503 BUSY and Retry-After before any database work; capacity returns when a request finishes; a cap below 1 is refused.

in a real browser the page follows the API's bounded shapes: an identity's fields in keyset pages (100 rows, the field count, 'load more fields' with the API's cursor), a group's first 100 members with its member count on the identity and contract views, a 200-byte entry point drawn as its first 128 bytes with its length.

an unresolved log of a contract (a rename or withdrawal the raw transaction does not show) takes the clean mark from every identity of that contract: list rows, identity detail, color, lookup and contract views answer 'unresolved' with the reason unresolved-log, the count and the positions (first 100 of many); with a rejected event as well the mark is 'incorrect' and its reasons end with unresolved-log; another contract keeps 'ok'.

100 000 metadata transactions of a withdrawn identity behind one visible rejected event, and 100 000 visible ones of a sibling: with no statistics, with statistics taken while the listed events held two live rows on pages that later fill again, and with fresh statistics, the color's and the contract's activity pages in both orders read at most 100 + 20 buffers per row a page may read (auto_explain); in the stale state the listing's skip-scan step and a primary-key lookup planned without the listings' settings read the whole listed table (negative control); before the first vacuum after the withdrawal, its dead index entries add at most one buffer per 20 hidden rows; the API answers within a generous latency budget; the fast seeding equals the real apply path on a small count; the withdrawal that hides 100 000 listed rows is one bounded delete.
the import walk from the runtime entry modules resolves every relative import and reaches the core modules
no runtime module imports a Node module or uses Buffer or another Node-only global (allow-list aside)
every allow-listed module is scanned and still uses a Node API (an entry it no longer needs fails here)
the browser build's worker and page never load the PostgreSQL client (postgres.js), not even through a dynamic import
Node tooling exists and no runtime module imports it
negative control: the rules flag every Node API shape and nothing in comments or strings
nests fragments, conditional and empty fragments and arrays of fragments, numbering parameters in order
reuses one fragment in several statements and inlines unsafe text used as a fragment
quotes identifiers, each part of a dotted name, and escapes quotes
infers the type oids postgres.js sends: Date 1184, bytes 17, boolean 16, bigint 20, json 3802, arrays by element; others 0
builds insert column lists and value rows from objects, rows and named columns
builds update assignments, values lists, in lists (empty: null), select lists and returning lists
compiles unsafe text with parameters after the text, and refuses an undefined value
awaiting an identifier or a helper value is refused as a non-tagged call
serializes parameters by their described type and returns arrays with count, command and columns
runs unsafe text with several statements (the last result) and unsafe text with parameters
passes the parsers option to every statement and the error of PGlite through mapError (normalized by default)
cursors, forEach, values, raw, describe, streams, cancel and listen are not supported
gives every client its own search_path, also for concurrent statements and transactions
writes the begin, commit, rollback and savepoint statements postgres.js writes
rolls a savepoint back to itself when its callback fails, keeping the transaction
rolls back when the callback throws, and when a statement failed even though the callback caught it
refuses a statement on a transaction handle after the transaction ended
refuses BEGIN as a plain statement (only begin, reserve or a transaction handle start transactions)
transaction handles have savepoint and no begin; top-level clients have begin and no savepoint; reserved handles neither
reserve() holds the session for its own statements until release(); RESET search_path returns to the client's schema
a statement on the outer client awaited inside a transaction fails with PGLITE_SESSION_DEADLOCK instead of hanging
a statement waiting behind a transaction that keeps running statements waits as long as needed
runs waiting statements in arrival order
a failed array-type load fails the statement and is retried by the next one
validates the schema and the deadlock timeout
end() waits for the client's pending statements, then refuses new ones; the database stays open unless the client owns it
openPgliteClient opens an in-memory database that end() closes
int8 is always a bigint (also in int8[]), numeric the decimal text, bytea the bytes, on both backends

the single PGlite session: a statement that can never get it fails with PGLITE_SESSION_DEADLOCK, a database error (503), passed through unchanged by the error catalog
normalizePgliteError: PGlite's own error is recognized by shape too; non-database values pass unchanged
classifiers: PGlite is recognized by its version string; fsync=off in the non-durable mode is a warning on PGlite and a violation elsewhere
a client is non-durable by default: fsync=off is accepted as a non-durable warning, the chain-archive and MIP-0018 migrations run
a durable client keeps the PostgreSQL rule: fsync=off is refused before any migration runs
with fsync on, both modes pass with no warning and the probe sends the same statements as on PostgreSQL
openPgliteClient: non-durable by default (PGlite's fsync=off); a durable client's database starts with fsync on; a bad mode is refused
a PostgreSQL client is durable; fsync=off is refused, also for a client that claims the non-durable mode (the server is not PGlite)
on a healthy server a client claiming the non-durable mode has nothing to accept: no warning, migrations run
runs the chain-archive and mip0018 migrations through the migration runner (durability probe, reserve, BEGIN/COMMIT, unsafe DDL) with the same statements
archives the recorded IDX and U1 ranges with the sync service, sending the same statements
scans both ranges with the same statements and leaves every archive and mip0018 table equal; the recorded live-range digest holds on PostgreSQL
reads and writes through the rest of the archive store (blobs by role, verifier keys, canonical flips, lookups by height and hash) with the same statements and results
bytea[] NULL elements: postgres.js reads them as an empty Buffer, PGlite as null; unnest gives NULL on both
answers every API route with the same responses and statements, one request at a time and concurrently
reads through top-level clients (activity listings in their own read-only transactions, events, tokens) with the same results and statements
answers the 110 MIP-0018 vector requests through the PostgreSQL write and read path (a fresh migrated schema per request) with the same statements and answers
removes the scan above a height (event replay) and rescans with the same statements and tables; recomputing the fields changes nothing
every route and every error envelope (400, 404, 405, HEAD) answers identically on both backends
a database that cannot be read answers 503 UNAVAILABLE identically on both backends, the cause in the log only: an ended client, a missing schema
failures only PGlite has answer 503 UNAVAILABLE: a closed database, the single session held too long, PGlite's own error class; another error stays 500 INTERNAL

/v1/status reports the durability mode: durable on PostgreSQL and for a durable PGlite client, non-durable for a PGlite client in the default mode; the handler option overrides it; anything else is refused
a new archive starts at the finalized tip both sources serve, waits with back-off while they fail (never genesis), follows the tip, and a later engine catches up the gap from its cursor
a stop while the engine waits for the tip ends the sync cleanly; an invalid start height is refused

a snapshot of an engine that synced and scanned the recorded U1 range validates against the schema, and every value equals its source: heights, scanner, unresolved events, durability and build references equal /v1/status; table sizes, row estimates, exact counts, database size, server version, fsync and migrations equal the catalog; per-endpoint requests equal the fake chain's; scan totals equal the scan events; the configuration shows the engine's effective options

the statistics are read one autocommit statement at a time — no transaction, reservation or multi-statement text, never two at once — each one timed; on PGlite another request's transaction runs on the session between two of them and none runs inside one

collection follows the viewers: nothing while no one watches (no statement, no request, no timer); a viewer gets a snapshot at once, then one every 2 s with the catalog read again every 30 s; when the last viewer leaves collection stops, and a new viewer starts it again; a refresh on demand still works

the health line follows the engine: catching up while the archive and the scan are behind the tip, following at the tip, waiting (network) while a call is retried and while the sync backs off after a network failure (with the last error and the next attempt), stalled (scan) after a failed scan step, paused (quota) from the host's storage reading, error from a fatal failure, stopped; watchdog restarts are counted; a follower shows the leader's snapshot

the diagnostics file holds no secret from hostile configuration, errors and log lines (URL credentials and query secrets, API keys, tokens, passwords, cookies), keeps hostile text as text (control, bidirectional and markup characters), validates against the schema and reads back equal; host data outside the schema (a browsing history) is refused

an instrumented fetch counts each request to the node and to the indexer (same origin and path): started, in flight, 2xx, 429, 403, 5xx, other statuses, no answer and aborted; other URLs are not counted; answers and rejections pass through unchanged; retries come from the sync's backoff events (indexer.* operations are the indexer's)

blocks per second over the last minute: each batch's blocks spread over the time since the loop's previous batch (or the sync's start), divided by the window or by the time since the start when shorter; totals since the start; the chain's seconds per block from the tip's rise
the API counters: answered requests by status class, BUSY refusals apart, and nearest-rank p50/p95 latency over the latest 1,000 admitted requests

the log ring keeps the latest 200 lines, newest first with increasing sequence numbers; every sync and scan event is a line except a batch of zero blocks; API requests are not lines, the handler's error lines are; text is kept as given (control, bidirectional and markup characters included) up to the length cap

the hooks a host calls: watchdog restarts (and counts carried from the previous worker), PGlite reopens that restart the failed-statement count since the open, failed statements in total, and a fatal failure; each hook leaves a log line

the network signals the health rule reads: a retry newer than the last batch means a call is being retried; a batch error after a retry, or after a failed request, failed on the network; a batch error with neither did not

the health line: error (fatal or a failed loop) before paused (quota) before stopped before stalled (scan) before waiting (network) before a non-network sync error, then running / catching up / following from the heights

the snapshot schema is versioned and strict: a complete snapshot validates; an unknown key at any depth, a missing section, a wrong version or more than 200 log lines is refused; a follower relays the leader's snapshot marked follower; the diagnostics file is the redacted snapshot as JSON

redaction removes secrets from hostile values — URL userinfo, query and fragment of any scheme, key=value / key: value / JSON members naming a secret, Authorization and Cookie headers, Bearer and Basic credentials, JWTs, Bech32m secret keys — idempotently, and keeps public chain data, data directories and ordinary messages

one engine syncs the recorded IDX range through an injected fetch (called as a plain function), scans it and answers the API: the archive digest equals the recorded live sync's, the 37 tables equal the recorded live range, every block is fetched once, and the events carry the sync's start, batches, range-complete and stop

a start-height function is asked only for a new archive, with the engine's signal; the archive, the scan and /v1/status start there; a later engine on the same store resumes at the cursor without asking and reports the archive's own first height

the loops wait through the injected clock: the sync at the tip waits sync.idleMs and the scan at the archive's tip scan.idleMs; a failed batch backs off ×2 with injected jitter (750, 1500, 3000 for 1000 × 0.75) and resets after a success; a network call is retried through the same clock; a stalled scan backs off idleMs × 5^k up to 60 s, reports stalled in /v1/status and recovers

every sync batch and scan step goes through the injected scheduler and API requests never do; stop() during a held scan step resolves only after that step has written all its blocks, and no step starts after it

a sync start above cursor + 1 is refused (range-refused, then stop; finished rejects with SyncRangeError); drain mode ends at scan.toHeight or when caught up, and a failed drain step ends it (finished rejects, the error event has no retry)

handle() answers exactly as the API handler, also before start(), and reports each request (status, busy, duration); the request cap answers 503 BUSY while requests are in flight; the handler's error lines arrive as api log events
options are checked when the engine is made; start() runs once; without loops start() and stop() do nothing and the cursors are undefined; an aborted signal stops the loops; a listener can be removed
the reported finalized height rises with the injected clock (by blocks every everyMs, up to until), moves by hand, and node and indexer report the same height
replaying each recorded range through the fetch-shaped tape replay, with no HTTP server, reproduces the live sync's archive digest (IDX cb0d5e21…, U1 fa89d909…)
a sync with no end height follows a finalized tip that rises with a clock: each round ingests up to the tip of that moment, never past it, and the finished archive equals the live U1 archive

the node:http fake chain and the fetch-shaped replay (and the fake chain's fetch transport) give identical answers (status, content-type, retry-after, body) to every request of the archive sync, the throttles and the error cases
every gzip copy matches its manifest's SHA-256 and size, names its fixture source by the fixture manifest's SHA-256, and decodes to byte-identical JSON (node:zlib and DecompressionStream alike)

the default build: engine.html opens its head with the policy (inline style by its SHA-256) and no-referrer; _headers gives every path the same policy plus frame-ancestors, cross-origin isolation and hardening headers; connect-src is the site and the two Stagenet origins; no unsafe-eval or unsafe-inline

every HTML input gets the policy with its own inline hashes, _headers admits their union, the prelude runs first in each page; inline event handlers, style attributes and javascript: URLs fail the build
the chain comes from UMBRADB_BROWSER_* (https, or http on a loopback host, no credentials, a network id); a build configured with other endpoints admits exactly their origins and carries them
accepts only a same-origin script inside the loading module's directory, is created once under its allowed name, and hands the Worker constructor its result

with the _headers rules: page and worker are cross-origin isolated; the worker boots on OPFS, replays and scans a recorded range and answers API requests with no CSP violation in the page or the worker, and every request stays on the site's origin; a second tab follows through the leader with the same answers and no violation
a build configured with a chain on another origin: the sync reads it cross-origin under COEP with no violation, and the requests are the site's and that origin's only
with no headers, the page's meta policy alone: the same boot, replay and API answers with no violation and only same-origin requests

in both forms: an inline script without a hash does not run; eval and new Function are refused in the page (and in a worker under the header policy) while WebAssembly compiles; a fetch outside the policy is refused and never arrives; a Worker from a string, another Trusted Types policy and an HTML sink are refused; each refusal is reported
boots through capabilities, store, ledger and migrate to ready; both schema lineages are migrated; the API answers before any start

a malformed message gets bad-request, another version unsupported-version, an unknown type unknown-type; export and import answer not-implemented; a first start with no start height begins at the finalized tip
start syncs and scans the replayed range; stop leaves both cursors at a full block; a restart continues at the cursor
a network source: every height is fetched once across a stop and a restart
an unsupported browser opens no store and starts nothing; a ledger build with renamed classes fails the boot and closes the store
Chrome with OPFS sync access handles, Web Locks, BroadcastChannel and persistent storage is supported; each missing piece is named in a Chrome-only refusal

the client turns requests into validated results over a message channel: errors carry the worker's code, notices reach listeners, invalid messages are reported and dropped, close rejects what is pending
the catalog's files and SHA-256 values are the tapes' manifest; a tape that does not match its hash is refused
digest gives the archive digest and the digest of every table of both schemas in one transaction; the replayed U1 range gives the recorded live archive digest

a start with no start height begins at the finalized tip; a start with no configuration runs the saved one; a reopened store resumes at its cursor through the gap; a stop turns the automatic start off
range drops the data and starts the new range; reset runs it again to the same digests; range tip follows again; a reopened store keeps the range's end
the sync pauses before the quota (paused (quota)), a stop while paused returns at once, and it resumes once the usage is back under the threshold minus the margin
with the default Stagenet endpoints, request starts are 250 ms apart per endpoint and a 429's Retry-After is honoured

a ready worker's status always carries a storage reading: the first is taken before ready without waiting for the store's walk; a silent estimate counts as unknown; a walk that never ends delays neither readings nor the pause

the leader resumes the previous leader's running configuration, else starts the saved configuration when it says to start by itself, else nothing; with the build's automatic start off it starts only a previous leader's
the IDX and U1 ranges replayed in the worker on OPFS give the recorded live archive digests, and IDX the recorded live range's digest of every table of both schemas

an empty profile starts at the finalized tip with no input, waits while the endpoints fail (never genesis), follows the advancing tip, resumes through the gap after a reopen, pauses before the quota, and range, reset and stop behave as specified
with two tabs exactly one worker runs, in the leader tab, and alone holds the store; the follower starts none, starts the engine through the leader, and gets identical answers

closing the leader while its sync waits for the next height: the follower leads, boots its own worker on the same store, resumes the same configuration from the stored cursors, fetches no stored height again and every later one once, and ends with the uninterrupted run's answers

requests in flight to a frozen leader when it closes: reads are answered by the next leader, also for a third tab; state changes fail with leader-changed; the next leader resumes the replay in its worker to the end

the first tab leads and alone starts a worker; the others follow; when the leader closes the oldest follower leads and the rest follow it; presence counts open tabs; without Web Locks or BroadcastChannel a tab runs alone

a follower's requests, reads and state changes alike, are answered by the leader's engine as the leader's own are; errors keep the leader's code; notices reach followers; a relayed system snapshot is marked relayed

in flight when the leader closes: status, api and export are answered by the next leader, other requests fail leader-changed, a late answer from the old leader is ignored; with no leader a request fails leader-unavailable; the new leader resumes the running engine, and only then
invalid tab messages are reported and ignored; the leader refuses an unknown request type; closing rejects what is pending and releases the tab's locks
the store lock admits one holder; the next waits for its release; a wait that runs out fails naming the store
the build holds one ledger-v9 instance with its class names kept, PGlite's assets and both tapes; the node-free plugin refuses postgres.js and Node built-ins
the worker boots on OPFS, syncs and scans a replayed range, survives reloads with the same cursors and API answers, and resumes at the cursor fetching only the missing heights
the worker answers malformed and unknown messages with their error codes, refuses a second start, and answers not-implemented for export and import

the 110 vector requests (59/59 reference normative, 43/43 informative, 8/8 UmbraDB versions) answered through the PGlite store in a worker on OPFS in Chrome pass with every check applicable, and every answer equals the pure consumer's

through the engine worker's API, each recorded case replayed in the worker only up to its own last block (and C06 at each step) equals its expectation while every later case is still absent; earlier cases stay equal; U1 at its last block

through the engine worker's API at the end of IDX and U1: the reference index's colors (first and last mint, mint count, amount), v1-named events (position, segment, phase, classification, reason) and range, and IDX/expected.json's colors through /v1/lookup; exactly 6 colors in IDX

through the engine worker's API: every case identity's mark (and C06's after each step) equals the mark rule applied to the reference expectations and the reference index's rejections; the third party's minted token has no mark; every case contract's metadata transactions are the reference index's, with their counts; C05 bronze, never minted, has no color

every answer of a crawl of the API (every listing page, color, lookup, identity field page, contract, event page and transaction, activity pages in both orders, error answers, HEAD and a refused method) from the engine worker equals the Node handler's over the same range synced and scanned in Node: status, headers and body, /v1/status apart from durability

a snapshot from the worker validates against the schema and equals its sources: heights equal /v1/status, storage equals navigator.storage, table sizes, estimates, exact counts and database size equal the catalog read from the store by another page, the configuration shows the build, the watchdog limit, the data directory and the browser; watched it arrives every 2 s, unwatched nothing is collected
a follower tab watches the leader's snapshots through the leader and gets them marked follower; closing it without unwatching releases its viewer, and the leader's worker stops collecting

the worker's thread held busy during the IDX replay is terminated after the limit and grace; the API request in flight gets the 503; a new worker continues at the stored cursors to the recorded digests; the snapshot counts the restart
the page's API round trips are bounded while the worker replays the IDX range (sync and scan running), and measured with the engine stopped

one turn of the event loop per time slice while statements run back to back; statements and database failures counted (with their SQLSTATE), a closed database is not a failed statement; the statement in flight is known
closing waits for the statements in flight and refuses new ones (the client answers CONNECTION_CLOSED); PGlite closes once they have ended

while the IDX range replays, a page's API requests are answered between block transactions with a bounded round trip; without the time slices they wait for whole steps; the tables are the same either way

at 1,000 failed statements since the store was opened PGlite is reopened: requests are held, the engine stops at a full block and continues with the same configuration, and the replay ends with the same tables as an uninterrupted one; the reopen is counted and the failed statements start again from zero

with the count rule off PGlite's own defect appears (every statement fails with stack depth limit exceeded, 54001) after about 1,870 failures; the first such failure reopens the store at once and the engine continues to the same tables

a refreshed snapshot validates against the schema and every value equals its source: heights and scanner equal /v1/status, table sizes, estimates, exact counts and database size equal the catalog, storage equals the storage reading, endpoint requests equal the chain's counts, the configuration shows the running engine, the watchdog limit, the build and the data directory; the diagnostics file reads back equal

the page follows snapshots while visible: a notice every interval while watched; hidden or gone (pagehide) nothing is collected — no statement, no notice; visible again it resumes; collection runs until the last of two viewers leaves

after a watchdog request the worker posts a heartbeat every interval with the counts a replacing worker carries; carried counts show in the snapshot and the log; a new request changes the interval; closing the host ends the heartbeat
an API request in flight on a restart gets exactly the API handler's 503 UNAVAILABLE answer, for GET and HEAD

a statement that does not return silences the worker; the page terminates it and starts a new one: the API request in flight gets the 503, a status request restarted; the new worker carries the counts, continues the engine at the cursors, and the range ends with the same tables

a late check is not a restart when the worker answers within the grace; a silent worker is restarted once with the viewers and the engine restored; an engine the page stopped stays stopped; a boot failing right after a restart is retried; too many restarts close the client
while a reset is in flight the worker may stay silent up to the longer limit; past it the worker is restarted and the reset fails restarted

the IDX range replayed in the worker: the explorer's route checks of the Node page pass with the API answered by the engine; 'history before block H is not indexed' next to the lists and in the panel; one module script; only same-origin requests, none to /v1; the font loaded; no CSP violation in the page or the worker, no exception or console error
the explorer's recorded activity checks of the Node page pass with the API answered by the engine; only same-origin requests; no CSP violation, exception or console error

C06 step by step with the page open and refreshing on its own, the engine replaying the IDX tape up to each step: the withdrawn name is on no reachable view after the tombstone and stays absent after the revive; no CSP violation

through the engine: an answer announced or streamed over 8 MiB is TOO_LARGE, a 503 is its error code, a failed engine request is UNREACHABLE (each as a fetched answer is rendered); hostile text in an engine answer is drawn as marks and markup as text, no script runs; no CSP violation

the engine panel: empty store, then the start height and its 'history before' sentence next to the lists, heights, durability, configuration and storage; a second tab is marked follower; each control sends its one request (range with the typed heights, import with the chosen file), a drop of data first offers the export and cancel sends nothing; the engine's answers are shown; the follower is marked leader when the leader closes; the system status link; no CSP violation

the explorer's host answers a /v1 path with the engine's answer as a fetch Response: status, headers (content-length included) and body; it asks the engine GET of the path when called; a failed engine request rejects; the host asks for the start-height notes

the panel's view: every engine state with its detail, the first indexed height as 'history before block H is not indexed', the configuration in words, storage from the engine's reading (or the page's until there is one), the role and open tabs, the held range a drop would lose, and the typed range checked before it is sent

index.html is the /ui page's markup with one module script and stylesheets (no inline block) under the page policy; the bundle carries the explorer script, not the Node page module; the brand font and icon are emitted with the explorer's bytes; the plugin refuses a page style without its font reference and a doubled marker
a snapshot file is a tar of manifest.json and data.tar.gz; anything else, or a manifest this engine cannot take, is refused with its reason
a store exported at height H and imported into a new store holds the same data; the saved configuration continues the archive; a start requests H + 1 first and finishes as an uninterrupted run
exports taken while the sync and the scan write are each one state of the store
snapshots of another network, genesis block, schema version or PGlite version, changed, cut short, not a snapshot, or contradicting their manifest are refused with the reason, and nothing changes
an import journal is finished before PGlite opens the store; an invalid one is dropped; a snapshot that fails to load leaves an empty store; a host booting over a journal reports the import
the published snapshot of 714485–715183 holds the recorded live sync, its index validates, and an import of it answers the API with no chain request
export after replaying IDX, import into a new profile: equal digests and API answers; a partial snapshot continues at its height + 1 to the same digests
snapshots of another network, schema version or PGlite version, changed or cut short are refused by the worker with their reasons; the store is unchanged
the build's published IDX snapshot, made in Node, boots the explorer API in a new profile with no chain request and no CSP violation
a follower tab exports and imports through the leader: the snapshot file crosses BroadcastChannel both ways
the explorer's engine panel exports the store as a download and a new profile's panel imports that file: equal digests
an import journal beside a damaged store is finished by the next boot before PGlite opens the store
